chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi':
He said: I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) enter the grave without undoing his buttons.

The interpretation of this report is the lifting of the prohibition upon whoever does not undo his buttons, because doing so is among the recommended acts (masnnunat) and not among the obligatory acts (wajibat).

key_terms.أَزْرَارَهُ: his buttons/clasps — the closures of a garment whose undoing before entering the grave is a recommended sunnah
key_terms.الْمَسْنُونَاتِ: recommended (sunnah) acts — practices established by the sunnah that are rewarded if performed but not sinful if omitted
key_terms.الْوَاجِبَاتِ: obligatory acts — mandatory religious duties whose omission incurs sin
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْحَظْرِ: lifting of the prohibition — a jurisprudential term indicating that an omission is permissible and not forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory or merely a recommended sunnah to undo one's garment buttons when entering the grave during burial?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' witnessed Abu al-Hasan (AS) — likely Imam al-Ridha or Imam al-Kadhim — enter a grave during burial rites without undoing the buttons of his garment. Sheikh al-Tusi (the author of al-Istibsar) cites this report to clarify that undoing one's buttons before entering the grave is a recommended sunnah practice, not an obligation, and therefore omitting it carries no sin.
